theme: Instruments for determining length or distance.
decoy: Measuring and layout tools used in a workshop or on a job site

members.title: Tape measure
members.description: Spring-retracting steel ribbon in a case, with a hooked tip.

members.title: Micrometer
members.description: C-shaped frame with a finely threaded spindle and rotating thimble.

members.title: Caliper
members.description: Sliding jaws on a graduated beam for gauging parts inside and out.

members.title: Folding rule
members.description: Hinged wooden segments that open out into one rigid stick.

members.title: Feeler gauge
members.description: Fan of thin steel blades, each stamped with its thickness.

members.title: Measuring wheel
members.description: Wheel on a long handle that clicks off each turn along the ground.

members.title: Laser rangefinder
members.description: Handheld unit that bounces a beam off a far wall.

members.title: Odometer
members.description: Dashboard counter tallying how far a vehicle has traveled.

members.title: Surveyor's chain
members.description: Sixty-six-foot run of iron links used in early land surveys.

intruders.title: Chalk line
intruders.description: Reel of powdered string in a case, snapped taut on a board.
intruders.why: It only marks a straight line between two points and measures nothing. The string reels into a case like a tape measure, which is why it looks like one.

intruders.title: Plumb bob
intruders.description: Pointed brass weight hung on a string over a mark on the floor.
intruders.why: It establishes true vertical but gives no reading of how long anything is. It sits in every layout kit beside the rules and tapes.

theme: Laboratory vessels that are traditionally made of glass.
decoy: Standard chemistry-lab vessels and apparatus

members.title: Beaker
members.description: Straight-sided cylinder with a pouring lip and rough volume marks.

members.title: Conical flask
members.description: Flat-bottomed container tapering to a narrow neck for swirling.

members.title: Test tube
members.description: Slim round-bottomed tube held in racks or clamped over a flame.

members.title: Graduated cylinder
members.description: Tall narrow column marked for measuring out liquid volumes.

members.title: Burette
members.description: Long marked tube with a stopcock, dispensing titrant drop by drop.

members.title: Volumetric flask
members.description: Pear-shaped bulb with a long neck bearing a single fill line.

members.title: Round-bottom flask
members.description: Spherical container that rests in a cork ring or heating mantle.

members.title: Liebig condenser
members.description: Jacketed tube cooled by circulating water to turn vapor to liquid.

members.title: Volumetric pipette
members.description: Thin tube with a central bulb that delivers one exact volume.

intruders.title: Crucible
intruders.description: Small heat-resistant cup, often with a lid, for heating samples hard.
intruders.why: Normally porcelain, other ceramic, or metal such as platinum, since glass would soften at those temperatures. It sits among the flasks on every chemistry bench.

intruders.title: Buchner funnel
intruders.description: Funnel with a flat perforated plate, fitted to a flask for filtering.
intruders.why: Classically made of glazed porcelain (glass and plastic versions came later). It is always mounted on a glass flask, so it reads as glassware.

intruders.title: Evaporating dish
intruders.description: Shallow round bowl with a pouring lip, used to boil off solvent.
intruders.why: Traditionally glazed porcelain, which tolerates direct heating. It looks like a watch glass or a small beaker.

theme: Tools that drive or set fasteners into place.
decoy: Hand and power tools for working with staples, nails, rivets and screws

members.title: Stapler
members.description: Desktop device with a spring-loaded magazine and a hinged top.

members.title: Nail gun
members.description: Pneumatic or cordless gun fed by a strip of collated nails.

members.title: Staple gun
members.description: Heavy trigger-fired gun for tacking sheeting and upholstery to wood.

members.title: Pop rivet gun
members.description: Squeeze-handled gun that pulls a mandrel until it snaps off.

members.title: Impact driver
members.description: Compact cordless driver that adds rotary hammer blows for torque.

members.title: Hog ring pliers
members.description: Grooved-jaw pliers that close metal rings around wire or fabric.

members.title: Grommet setter
members.description: Punch-and-anvil pair that flares a metal eyelet through canvas.

members.title: Cable tie gun
members.description: Pistol-grip device that tensions plastic straps and trims the tail.

members.title: Tack hammer
members.description: Light hammer with a magnetized face that holds small tacks.

intruders.title: Staple remover
intruders.description: Pair of interlocking steel claws on a spring hinge, kept on desks.
intruders.why: It pries staples out, the opposite job. It lives beside the stapler, so it looks like part of the set.

intruders.title: Cat's paw
intruders.description: Short steel bar with a curved, notched claw at one end.
intruders.why: A nail puller that digs out driven nails, so it removes fasteners rather than setting them. It belongs to the same framing toolkit as the nail gun.

intruders.title: Screw extractor
intruders.description: Hardened bit with a reverse spiral, chucked into a cordless drill.
intruders.why: It backs out broken or stripped screws, which is removal, not installation. It is chucked like a driver bit.

theme: Instruments that measure an electrical quantity such as current, voltage, resistance or power.
decoy: Meters with needle or digital readouts

members.title: Ammeter
members.description: Meter wired in series into a circuit, often with a moving needle.

members.title: Voltmeter
members.description: Meter connected across two points, with high internal impedance.

members.title: Ohmmeter
members.description: Meter that checks a component using its own internal battery.

members.title: Multimeter
members.description: Handheld box with a rotary selector and red and black probes.

members.title: Galvanometer
members.description: Sensitive needle meter built around a coil in a magnet's field.

members.title: Wattmeter
members.description: Meter pairing a fixed coil and a moving coil to gauge a load.

members.title: Oscilloscope
members.description: Screen that plots a signal's waveform against time.

members.title: Clamp meter
members.description: Jawed handheld meter closed around a single cable.

members.title: Electricity meter
members.description: Utility box on an outside wall that tallies kilowatt-hours.

intruders.title: Light meter
intruders.description: Handheld photocell meter that photographers use to set exposure.
intruders.why: It measures light intensity. It has a photocell and a needle, so it looks electrical, but light is what it reads.

intruders.title: Sound level meter
intruders.description: Handheld meter with a microphone that reads loudness in decibels.
intruders.why: It measures sound pressure. It has electronics and a meter display, but the quantity it reports is acoustic.

theme: Countertop kitchen appliances that cook or heat food or drink.
decoy: Plug-in countertop kitchen appliances

members.title: Toaster
members.description: Slotted box that browns bread slices and pops them up.

members.title: Slow cooker
members.description: Ceramic crock with a lid, left on for hours to braise stews.

members.title: Rice cooker
members.description: Lidded pot that switches itself to keep-warm when grains are done.

members.title: Waffle iron
members.description: Hinged plates with a grid pattern that close over batter.

members.title: Air fryer
members.description: Basket unit that blasts hot air to crisp fries and wings.

members.title: Electric kettle
members.description: Jug on a powered base that switches off at the boil.

members.title: Sous vide circulator
members.description: Stick-shaped unit clipped to a pot to hold a bath at a set temperature.

members.title: Panini press
members.description: Ridged hinged plates that flatten and toast filled sandwiches.

members.title: Bread machine
members.description: Box with a single pan that kneads, proofs and bakes a loaf.

members.title: Deep fryer
members.description: Oil-filled tub with a lowering basket and a thermostat.

intruders.title: Stand mixer
intruders.description: Tilt-head machine with a bowl, beaters and a dough hook.
intruders.why: It mixes and kneads but has no heating element. It works the same dough as the bread machine, which does bake.

intruders.title: Ice cream maker
intruders.description: Churning machine with a frozen bowl or built-in compressor.
intruders.why: It chills rather than warms. It is a plug-in dessert machine that sits on the same counter.

theme: Devices whose working action comes from a threaded screw.
decoy: Devices for clamping, pressing or lifting

members.title: Bench vise
members.description: Heavy jaws bolted to a workbench, closed by turning a long handle.

members.title: C-clamp
members.description: Forged C-shaped frame with a swivel pad pressed by a turned handle.

members.title: Corkscrew
members.description: Pointed helix on a handle that pulls stoppers from wine bottles.

members.title: Scissor jack
members.description: Diamond-shaped car jack cranked by a rod through its middle.

members.title: Turnbuckle
members.description: Metal link with opposing ends that tightens a cable when rotated.

members.title: Hose clamp
members.description: Slotted steel band tightened around tubing by a small head.

members.title: Meat grinder
members.description: Hand-cranked hopper that forces meat against a perforated plate.

members.title: Pipe clamp
members.description: Fittings mounted on a length of pipe to squeeze glued boards.

members.title: Book press
members.description: Iron frame with a platen lowered by a wheel onto stacked books.

intruders.title: Spring clamp
intruders.description: Hand-squeezed clamp with plastic-tipped jaws and a coiled hinge.
intruders.why: A coiled spring supplies the grip and there is no thread anywhere. It does the same job as the C-clamp.

intruders.title: Toggle clamp
intruders.description: Lever clamp bolted to a jig that locks when pushed past center.
intruders.why: It holds by an over-center linkage, not a thread. It clamps work just like the vise and C-clamp.

intruders.title: Hydraulic jack
intruders.description: Squat bottle-shaped car jack pumped with a removable handle.
intruders.why: It lifts by oil pressure from a small pump plunger. It does the same job as the threaded scissor jack.

theme: Optical instruments that show an enlarged image of their subject.
decoy: Handheld or mounted devices you look through with one or both eyes

members.title: Compound microscope
members.description: Stage, objective turret and eyepiece stacked on a heavy stand.

members.title: Jeweler's loupe
members.description: Tiny folding lens held right up against the eye.

members.title: Magnifying glass
members.description: Single convex lens in a round frame on a handle.

members.title: Binoculars
members.description: Paired prism-folded tubes focused by a central wheel.

members.title: Opera glasses
members.description: Small paired viewers, often gilded, for watching a stage.

members.title: Spotting scope
members.description: Angled single tube on a tripod for birding and target shooting.

members.title: Rifle scope
members.description: Tube with crosshairs clamped on top of a hunting rifle.

members.title: Monocular
members.description: Pocket-sized single tube for glimpsing distant signs or birds.

intruders.title: Kaleidoscope
intruders.description: Mirror-lined tube of colored chips, turned against the light.
intruders.why: Its mirrors multiply the view into symmetric patterns and nothing is enlarged. It is a tube held to one eye, like a monocular.

intruders.title: Door peephole
intruders.description: Tiny lens tube fitted through a front door at eye level.
intruders.why: Its wide-angle lens shrinks the scene so the whole doorstep fits in view, which gives a reduced image. You look through its lens as you would a loupe.

theme: Tools that grind food into powder, paste or small particles.
decoy: Traditional hand-operated kitchen implements

members.title: Mortar and pestle
members.description: Heavy bowl worked with a short club-shaped pounder.

members.title: Pepper mill
members.description: Tall tabletop shaker turned by hand, adjusted by a top knob.

members.title: Burr grinder
members.description: Coffee machine with two ridged discs set at an adjustable gap.

members.title: Quern
members.description: Pair of round stones, the upper one turned by a wooden handle.

members.title: Molcajete
members.description: Three-legged basalt bowl used for salsas and guacamole.

members.title: Suribachi
members.description: Japanese ceramic bowl with a combed, ridged interior.

members.title: Metate
members.description: Sloped stone slab worked with a hand stone over maize.

members.title: Poppy seed mill
members.description: Crank mill clamped to a table in Central European kitchens.

intruders.title: Tortilla press
intruders.description: Two hinged flat plates, often cast iron, closed with a lever.
intruders.why: It flattens balls of dough into discs and breaks nothing down. It is used alongside the metate in the same kitchens.

intruders.title: Meat mallet
intruders.description: Weighted hammer with a studded face for kitchen work.
intruders.why: It pounds cuts thin to tenderize them but reduces nothing to powder or paste. It is swung like a pestle.

theme: Instruments that measure angles.
decoy: Instruments with pivoting arms or arcs, used in drafting, layout, surveying and navigation

members.title: Protractor
members.description: Half-disc of clear plastic marked from zero to one hundred eighty.

members.title: Sextant
members.description: Brass arc with a swinging arm and mirrors for sighting the noon sun.

members.title: Theodolite
members.description: Tripod-mounted telescope that turns about two perpendicular axes.

members.title: Inclinometer
members.description: Device that reads the tilt of a slope, a pipe or a vehicle.

members.title: Goniometer
members.description: Hinged pair of arms that physiotherapists lay along a joint.

members.title: Astrolabe
members.description: Engraved brass disc with a rotating sighting bar called an alidade.

members.title: Bevel protractor
members.description: Steel dial with a swinging blade, used by machinists on workpieces.

members.title: Quadrant
members.description: Quarter-circle plate with a plumb line, used by early astronomers.

intruders.title: Sliding bevel
intruders.description: Adjustable steel blade locked to a wooden handle by a wing nut.
intruders.why: It copies and transfers a set slope but has no scale, so it measures nothing. Its name echoes the bevel protractor.

intruders.title: Drawing compass
intruders.description: Two hinged legs, one with a steel point and one holding a pencil.
intruders.why: It draws circles and steps off distances and has no scale for reading its opening. Its hinged legs make it look like an angle instrument.

theme: Scientific and calculating instruments first made in the 1600s.
decoy: Landmark instruments from the early centuries of modern science

members.title: Reflecting telescope
members.description: Tube that gathers light with a curved mirror instead of a lens.

members.title: Mercury barometer
members.description: Glass tube of quicksilver standing inverted in an open dish.

members.title: Pendulum clock
members.description: Timepiece regulated by a swinging weighted rod.

members.title: Slide rule
members.description: Sliding logarithmic scales for multiplying and dividing.

members.title: Napier's bones
members.description: Set of numbered rods for doing multiplication by lattice.

members.title: Pascaline
members.description: Brass box of geared dials that adds and subtracts numbers.

members.title: Vernier scale
members.description: Short sliding scale that reads between the marks of a main scale.

members.title: Air pump
members.description: Cylinder and piston for drawing air out of a sealed vessel.

intruders.title: Leyden jar
intruders.description: Foil-lined glass jar with a brass rod, for storing charge.
intruders.why: Invented in 1745-46 by Ewald von Kleist and, independently, Pieter van Musschenbroek at Leiden. It feels like early experimental apparatus of the air-pump era but is from the 1700s.

intruders.title: Achromatic telescope
intruders.description: Tube with a two-glass objective that cancels colored fringes.
intruders.why: Chester Moor Hall devised achromatic lenses around 1730 and John Dollond patented them in 1758. It sits naturally beside the 1600s reflecting telescope, which was a workaround for the same color problem.

theme: Programming languages and tools created at Bell Labs.
decoy: Influential languages and tools from the systems-software tradition

members.title: C
members.description: Terse compiled systems code with pointers and manual memory management.

members.title: C++
members.description: Adds classes, templates and destructors to a lower-level predecessor.

members.title: AWK
members.description: Pattern-action scripts for processing text files line by line.

members.title: SNOBOL
members.description: 1960s string-manipulation notation built around pattern matching.

members.title: Limbo
members.description: Concurrent code written for the Inferno operating system.

members.title: Alef
members.description: Concurrent systems code for early versions of the Plan 9 system.

members.title: Bourne shell
members.description: Command interpreter that became the scripting shell of Version 7 Unix.

members.title: S
members.description: Interactive statistics environment designed by John Chambers and colleagues.

members.title: Newsqueak
members.description: Concurrent notation built around channels for writing window systems.

intruders.title: Golang
intruders.description: Compiled code with goroutines, channels and fast builds, released in 2009.
intruders.why: Created at Google. Its designers Ken Thompson and Rob Pike were Bell Labs veterans and it descends from Newsqueak and Limbo, which is why it looks like it belongs.

intruders.title: R
intruders.description: Open-source statistics environment with a vast package archive called CRAN.
intruders.why: Created by Ross Ihaka and Robert Gentleman at the University of Auckland. It reimplements S, which was a Bell Labs language.

theme: Cooking vessels traditionally made of cast iron.
decoy: Traditional regional pots and pans

members.title: Dutch oven
members.description: Heavy lidded pot for braising, sometimes set right in campfire coals.

members.title: Tetsubin
members.description: Japanese kettle with a bumpy hobnail exterior and a swing handle.

members.title: Potjie
members.description: Round three-legged pot used over open fires in South Africa.

members.title: Aebleskiver pan
members.description: Stovetop pan with round wells for Danish spherical pancakes.

members.title: Takoyaki pan
members.description: Plate of half-sphere molds for octopus-filled batter balls.

members.title: Kazan
members.description: Deep round-bottomed cauldron used for plov in Central Asia.

members.title: Corn stick pan
members.description: Baking pan with molds shaped like small ears of maize.

members.title: Sukiyaki pan
members.description: Shallow pot for simmering sliced beef at the table in Japan.

intruders.title: Paella pan
intruders.description: Wide shallow two-handled pan for Valencian rice dishes.
intruders.why: Traditionally thin polished carbon steel, not cast iron. It is a heavy-looking dark regional pan cooked over open fire.

intruders.title: Cataplana
intruders.description: Clam-shaped hinged pan from the Algarve for seafood stews.
intruders.why: Traditionally hammered copper. It is a lidded regional vessel like the Dutch oven.

intruders.title: Tamagoyaki pan
intruders.description: Rectangular pan for rolling layered Japanese omelets.
intruders.why: Traditionally tin-lined copper. It is a specialty Japanese pan, like the takoyaki and sukiyaki pans.

theme: Instruments that detect or measure ionizing radiation.
decoy: Nuclear and particle physics laboratory apparatus

members.title: Geiger counter
members.description: Handheld tube-and-speaker unit that clicks faster near a source.

members.title: Cloud chamber
members.description: Box of supersaturated vapor in which particle trails appear.

members.title: Bubble chamber
members.description: Tank of superheated liquid photographed as particle tracks form.

members.title: Spark chamber
members.description: Stacked metal plates between which sparks mark particle paths.

members.title: Scintillation counter
members.description: Crystal that flashes when struck, paired with a photomultiplier tube.

members.title: Film badge
members.description: Clip-on packet of photographic film worn by hospital staff.

members.title: Wire chamber
members.description: Grid of fine charged wires that locates passing particles.

members.title: Proportional counter
members.description: Gas-filled tube whose pulse size scales with incoming energy.

members.title: Pocket dosimeter
members.description: Pen-sized quartz-fiber electrometer read by holding it to the light.

intruders.title: Cyclotron
intruders.description: Particle machine with two D-shaped electrodes inside a magnet.
intruders.why: It accelerates particles, producing beams rather than detecting radiation. It belongs to the same nuclear-physics labs.

intruders.title: Mass spectrometer
intruders.description: Instrument that sorts charged fragments by mass-to-charge ratio.
intruders.why: It identifies molecules and isotopes by mass; it is not a radiation detector. It uses ions and magnets like the particle apparatus.

theme: Equipment for twisting fiber into yarn or thread.
decoy: Hand tools and machines of textile production

members.title: Drop spindle
members.description: Weighted stick set whirling as it hangs from a lengthening strand.

members.title: Spinning wheel
members.description: Treadle-driven wheel and flyer found in cottage parlors.

members.title: Spinning jenny
members.description: Hand-cranked 1760s Lancashire frame working eight spindles at once.

members.title: Water frame
members.description: Arkwright's river-powered machine using rollers to draw out cotton.

members.title: Spinning mule
members.description: Crompton's machine on a moving carriage, combining two earlier ideas.

members.title: Charkha
members.description: Small hand-turned wheel that became a symbol of Indian independence.

members.title: Great wheel
members.description: Large hand-turned wheel worked while stepping back and forth.

members.title: Ring frame
members.description: Factory machine with a traveler circling each bobbin at high speed.

intruders.title: Flying shuttle
intruders.description: Wheeled boat-shaped carrier sent across a loom by pulling a cord.
intruders.why: John Kay's 1733 invention for weaving cloth, not making yarn. It is an Industrial Revolution textile landmark like the jenny and the mule.

intruders.title: Cotton gin
intruders.description: Toothed drum machine that pulls cotton lint away from its seeds.
intruders.why: It cleans raw cotton before any yarn is made. It is a famous textile machine of the same era.

theme: Mechanisms powered by a wound spring.
decoy: Clockwork mechanisms and mechanical timekeepers

members.title: Music box
members.description: Pinned cylinder plucks the teeth of a tuned steel comb.

members.title: Kitchen timer
members.description: Twist dial that ticks down and rings a bell at zero.

members.title: Mechanical wristwatch
members.description: Timepiece on a strap with a balance wheel and a crown.

members.title: Metronome
members.description: Pyramid-shaped case with a ticking inverted pendulum.

members.title: Gramophone
members.description: Horn-topped player for shellac discs with a side handle.

members.title: Clockwork radio
members.description: Receiver with a hand crank, designed for places without mains supply.

members.title: Carriage clock
members.description: Small brass-and-glass clock with a carrying handle on top.

members.title: Bolex H16
members.description: Swiss 16 mm cine camera that runs without any batteries.

members.title: Clockwork mouse
members.description: Tin toy that scurries across the floor when set down.

intruders.title: Cuckoo clock
intruders.description: Carved Black Forest wall clock with a bird that pops out.
intruders.why: Traditionally driven by cast-iron weights shaped like pine cones, hanging on chains. It is the archetypal clockwork novelty.

intruders.title: Longcase clock
intruders.description: Tall floor-standing clock with a long pendulum in its case.
intruders.why: Traditionally driven by hanging weights, not a spring. It is the classic mechanical timekeeper.

theme: Medical instruments for looking directly into the body through an opening or incision.
decoy: Diagnostic medical instruments whose names end in -scope

members.title: Otoscope
members.description: Lighted cone-tipped viewer a doctor aims into the ear.

members.title: Ophthalmoscope
members.description: Handheld light and lens set used to examine the retina.

members.title: Laryngoscope
members.description: Curved lighted blade used to expose the vocal cords.

members.title: Endoscope
members.description: Flexible tube with a camera fed down the digestive tract.

members.title: Bronchoscope
members.description: Thin tube passed down the windpipe into the airways.

members.title: Arthroscope
members.description: Pencil-thin camera probe used in keyhole knee surgery.

members.title: Cystoscope
members.description: Slim tube that urologists use to examine the bladder.

members.title: Colonoscope
members.description: Long flexible tube for inspecting the large intestine.

intruders.title: Stethoscope
intruders.description: Flexible Y-shaped tube a doctor presses to the chest.
intruders.why: It is for listening to the heart and lungs, not looking. It shares the -scope ending.

intruders.title: Fluoroscope
intruders.description: Imaging machine with a camera, used to watch organs move.
intruders.why: It images through the skin with X-rays, so nothing enters any opening. It does show the inside of the body in real time.

theme: Coffee brewers in which the water passes through the grounds by gravity alone.
decoy: Manual specialty-coffee brewing devices

members.title: Hario V60
members.description: Cone with spiral ribs and one large hole at its base.

members.title: Chemex
members.description: Hourglass-shaped glass carafe with a wooden collar and leather tie.

members.title: Kalita Wave
members.description: Flat-bottomed dripper with three small holes and fluted papers.

members.title: Melitta cone
members.description: Wedge-shaped filter holder that sits on top of a mug.

members.title: Vietnamese phin
members.description: Small steel cup with a perforated insert, set atop a glass.

members.title: Neapolitan flip pot
members.description: Two-chambered pot turned upside down once it reaches a boil.

members.title: Kyoto drip tower
members.description: Tall glass tower that makes cold brew slowly over many hours.

members.title: Nel drip
members.description: Flannel cloth filter on a wire handle, favored in Japanese kissaten.

intruders.title: Moka pot
intruders.description: Eight-sided aluminum stovetop pot in three screwed-together parts.
intruders.why: Steam pressure in the bottom chamber forces the water up through the grounds. It is a classic manual stovetop brewer.

intruders.title: AeroPress
intruders.description: Plastic syringe-like tube pushed down by hand into a mug.
intruders.why: Hand pressure on the plunger drives the water through. It sits on a mug like a dripper.

intruders.title: Siphon brewer
intruders.description: Two glass globes stacked one above the other over a burner.
intruders.why: Vapor pressure pushes water into the top globe, and a partial vacuum pulls the brew back down when the heat is removed. It is a showpiece of manual specialty brewing.

theme: Instruments that work by sensing fluid pressure, whatever units their dial shows.
decoy: Gauges used in flying, diving, weather, medicine and motoring

members.title: Aneroid altimeter
members.description: Cockpit gauge giving height above sea level in feet.

members.title: Airspeed indicator
members.description: Cockpit gauge fed by a forward-facing tube in the airstream.

members.title: Vertical speed indicator
members.description: Cockpit gauge giving rate of climb or descent in feet per minute.

members.title: Tire gauge
members.description: Pencil-sized stick gauge pressed onto a valve stem.

members.title: Sphygmomanometer
members.description: Inflatable arm cuff with a rubber bulb and a round gauge.

members.title: U-tube manometer
members.description: Bent liquid-filled tube whose two columns shift apart.

members.title: Bourdon gauge
members.description: Needle gauge driven by a curved flattened tube that uncoils.

members.title: Aneroid barometer
members.description: Wall gauge with a sealed metal capsule, marked Rain, Change, Fair.

members.title: Diving depth gauge
members.description: Wrist gauge telling a diver how far below the surface they are.

intruders.title: Radar altimeter
intruders.description: Cockpit gauge giving height above the terrain directly below.
intruders.why: It times a radio signal bounced off the ground. It reports altitude like the aneroid altimeter but senses no pressure.

intruders.title: Anemometer
intruders.description: Spinning cups on a mast whose turning rate gives wind speed.
intruders.why: It counts cup rotations. It reports air speed like the airspeed indicator but does not sense pressure.

theme: Weighing devices that compare the load with a known mass, so they read correctly under any gravity.
decoy: Scales for weighing goods, people and chemicals

members.title: Equal-arm balance
members.description: Beam pivoted at its center with a pan hanging from each end.

members.title: Steelyard
members.description: Unequal-armed bar with a hook and a sliding counterpoise.

members.title: Roberval balance
members.description: Two pans riding on a parallelogram linkage, as in old shops.

members.title: Triple beam balance
members.description: School-lab scale with three notched beams carrying riders.

members.title: Physician's beam scale
members.description: Upright doctor's office scale with sliding poises and a height rod.

members.title: Bismar
members.description: Rod with a fixed heavy knob at one end and a movable fulcrum.

members.title: Apothecary scale
members.description: Small brass two-pan scale in a glass case, for drug doses.

members.title: Kitchen balance
members.description: Enamel pan on one side and a platform for iron weights on the other.

intruders.title: Spring scale
intruders.description: Hook hanging from a marked cylinder with a sliding pointer.
intruders.why: It measures the force stretching a spring, so on the Moon it would read about one sixth of the Earth value. It is a classic weighing instrument.

intruders.title: Bathroom scale
intruders.description: Flat platform you stand on barefoot to check your weight.
intruders.why: Springs or strain-gauge load cells sense force, which depends on local gravity. It weighs people just like the physician's beam scale.

intruders.title: Digital kitchen scale
intruders.description: Slim flat pad with a tare button, used for measuring flour.
intruders.why: A strain-gauge load cell senses force, which depends on local gravity. It is a precision scale like the apothecary scale.

theme: Programming languages whose names began as acronyms or abbreviations.
decoy: Programming languages with names often written in capitals

members.title: COBOL
members.description: Verbose, English-like code behind decades of banking and payroll systems.

members.title: Fortran
members.description: IBM's 1950s numeric workhorse, long favored for scientific computing.

members.title: BASIC
members.description: Line-numbered code with GOTO that shipped on early home computers.

members.title: Lisp
members.description: Parenthesized code in which programs and data share one structure.

members.title: APL
members.description: Array notation written with a special set of mathematical symbols.

members.title: SQL
members.description: Declarative queries for selecting and joining rows in relational databases.

members.title: ALGOL
members.description: Committee design of 1958-60 that introduced nested block structure.

members.title: BCPL
members.description: Typeless 1960s Cambridge systems notation that paved the way for B and C.

members.title: Prolog
members.description: Logic-based code built from facts, rules and backtracking search.

members.title: Tcl
members.description: Embeddable scripting where everything is a string, often paired with Tk.

intruders.title: Perl
intruders.description: Text-processing scripting famed for regular expressions and a camel book.
intruders.why: The name came from 'Pearl' with a letter dropped. 'Practical Extraction and Report Language' is a backronym added afterward.

intruders.title: FORTH
intruders.description: Stack-based code in reverse Polish notation with user-defined words.
intruders.why: Chuck Moore meant 'fourth', but the IBM 1130 limited file names to five characters. It is often printed in capitals like an acronym.

intruders.title: LOGO
intruders.description: Educational code in which a turtle draws shapes on the screen.
intruders.why: Named from the Greek 'logos', meaning word or thought. It is often printed in capitals but is not an acronym.

theme: Tools whose name begins with the object they are used on.
decoy: Everyday hand tools with compound names

members.title: Screwdriver
members.description: Shaft with a flat or cross-shaped tip set in a grippy handle.

members.title: Nutcracker
members.description: Hinged pair of levers that crushes hard shells.

members.title: Can opener
members.description: Hand-cranked wheel that clamps onto a rim and pierces the lid.

members.title: Bottle opener
members.description: Flat metal piece with a lip that pries off crown caps.

members.title: Wire stripper
members.description: Plier-like device with graded notches that peel off insulation.

members.title: Pipe wrench
members.description: Heavy adjustable wrench with serrated jaws that bite harder under force.

members.title: Lug wrench
members.description: Cross-shaped or L-shaped bar kept in a car trunk for changing a wheel.

members.title: Tire lever
members.description: Flat spoon-ended bar for prying a bicycle bead off the rim.

members.title: Shoehorn
members.description: Curved slip of horn, metal or plastic that eases a heel into place.

members.title: Cherry pitter
members.description: Spring plunger that pushes the stones out of small fruit.

intruders.title: Monkey wrench
intruders.description: Adjustable wrench with smooth jaws set at right angles to the handle.
intruders.why: It is never used on monkeys; the first word is an unexplained nickname. Its two-word form matches pipe wrench and lug wrench.

intruders.title: Needle-nose pliers
intruders.description: Pliers with long tapering jaws for reaching into tight spaces.
intruders.why: 'Needle-nose' describes the shape of the jaws, not what they grip. It reads like 'wire stripper'.

intruders.title: Rat-tail file
intruders.description: Round tapering file for enlarging and smoothing holes.
intruders.why: The first word describes the file's shape. It reads like 'cherry pitter' or 'pipe wrench'.

theme: Devices whose working part relies on buoyancy in a liquid.
decoy: Devices for checking, measuring or controlling liquids

members.title: Hydrometer
members.description: Weighted glass stem with a scale, dropped into a sample jar.

members.title: Galileo thermometer
members.description: Sealed column of tagged glass bulbs that shift with the temperature.

members.title: Ballcock
members.description: Toilet cistern valve on an arm that shuts off when the tank is full.

members.title: Spirit level
members.description: Straight bar with a vial whose bubble centers when a surface is true.

members.title: Cartesian diver
members.description: Squeezable bottle holding a small dropper that dives on command.

members.title: Float switch
members.description: Sump pump trigger that flips on as the pit fills up.

members.title: Fishing bobber
members.description: Red-and-white ball on a line that dips when a fish bites.

members.title: Alcoholmeter
members.description: Distiller's glass gauge for checking the strength of spirits.

intruders.title: Refractometer
intruders.description: Handheld prism tube winemakers use to check sugar in grape juice.
intruders.why: It measures how much light bends in a drop of juice, and nothing floats. It does the same job as a hydrometer.

intruders.title: Pycnometer
intruders.description: Small glass flask with a capillary stopper, weighed empty and full.
intruders.why: It finds density by weighing an exact volume, and nothing floats. It does the same job as a hydrometer.

intruders.title: Dipstick
intruders.description: Long thin rod pulled from an engine to check the oil mark.
intruders.why: It shows level by the wetted mark and has no buoyant part, unlike a float gauge.

theme: Instruments that automatically record a measured quantity as a trace over time.
decoy: Devices whose names end in -graph

members.title: Seismograph
members.description: Suspended mass and pen that chart ground tremors on paper.

members.title: Barograph
members.description: Stack of aneroid capsules driving an inked arm across a slowly turning drum.

members.title: Polygraph
members.description: Bank of pens charting pulse, breathing and sweating during questioning.

members.title: Kymograph
members.description: Smoked revolving cylinder used in physiology labs since the 1840s.

members.title: Electrocardiograph
members.description: Machine with chest electrodes printing heartbeat waves on a strip.

members.title: Tachograph
members.description: Sealed truck unit logging speed and driving hours for regulators.

members.title: Sphygmograph
members.description: Nineteenth-century wrist device that drew the pulse as a wavy line.

members.title: Pluviograph
members.description: Rain gauge with a float and a pen that charts rainfall.

members.title: Hygrograph
members.description: Hair-driven stylus charting humidity on a weekly paper chart.

intruders.title: Heliograph
intruders.description: Tripod-mounted mirror that flashes sunlight in Morse code over miles.
intruders.why: A signaling device that sends messages and records nothing. It shares the -graph ending.

intruders.title: Pantograph
intruders.description: Linked parallelogram of rods and a pen that copies a drawing to scale.
intruders.why: It copies drawings with a pen but measures nothing. It shares the -graph ending and the pen-on-paper look.

intruders.title: Hectograph
intruders.description: Gelatin-pad duplicator that prints copies of a handwritten page.
intruders.why: A copying process for documents that measures nothing. It shares the -graph ending.

theme: Devices that draw in a second fluid through the low pressure of a fast-moving stream.
decoy: Sprayers, burners and fittings that mix or dispense liquids and gases

members.title: Carburetor
members.description: Engine part that mixes petrol and air, fitted with a choke and jets.

members.title: Perfume atomizer
members.description: Glass bottle with a squeezable rubber bulb and a fine nozzle.

members.title: Water aspirator
members.description: Tap-mounted lab fitting that provides suction for filtering.

members.title: Bunsen burner
members.description: Lab gas burner with an adjustable collar at the base of its barrel.

members.title: Airbrush
members.description: Pen-sized sprayer fed by a compressor, used for fine artwork.

members.title: Siphon-feed spray gun
members.description: Paint gun with a cup hanging beneath the nozzle.

members.title: Hose-end sprayer
members.description: Jar screwed to a garden hose for spreading fertilizer.

members.title: Steam injector
members.description: Valveless fitting that feeds water into a locomotive boiler.

members.title: Flit gun
members.description: Hand-pumped insecticide sprayer with a tank beneath the cylinder.

intruders.title: Aerosol can
intruders.description: Pressurized metal can with a push-down valve and a fine nozzle.
intruders.why: Compressed propellant pushes the product out; nothing is drawn in by a moving stream. It sprays a fine mist like the perfume atomizer.

intruders.title: Trigger spray bottle
intruders.description: Plastic bottle with a squeeze trigger, used for window cleaner.
intruders.why: A small piston pump pushes liquid straight out of the nozzle. It is a handheld sprayer like the flit gun.

theme: Direction-finding instruments that work by sensing Earth's magnetic field.
decoy: Compasses of every kind

members.title: Mariner's compass
members.description: Gimballed card in a binnacle on a ship's deck.

members.title: Lensatic compass
members.description: Folding military model with a sighting wire and a small lens.

members.title: Baseplate compass
members.description: Clear rectangular plate with a rotating bezel, used in orienteering.

members.title: Prismatic compass
members.description: Hand model with a prism for reading bearings while sighting.

members.title: Fluxgate compass
members.description: Electronic sensor with coils that feeds heading to an autopilot.

members.title: Whiskey compass
members.description: Liquid-filled standby unit mounted above a cockpit windshield.

members.title: Surveyor's compass
members.description: Brass dial with sight vanes, used to run property lines.

members.title: Thumb compass
members.description: Orienteering model worn on the thumb for quick map reading.

intruders.title: Gyrocompass
intruders.description: Motor-driven instrument that finds true north aboard large ships.
intruders.why: A spinning gyroscope aligns with the axis of Earth's rotation and ignores magnetism. It is the standard ship's compass.

intruders.title: Sun compass
intruders.description: Shadow-casting pin on a dial, used by desert patrols in vehicles.
intruders.why: It reads the sun's shadow. Desert patrols used it because steel vehicles upset magnetic needles.

intruders.title: Radio compass
intruders.description: Aircraft receiver whose needle points toward a ground beacon.
intruders.why: An automatic direction finder that homes on radio signals. It sits on the panel beside the magnetic compass.

theme: Devices that sort mixtures by density, letting heavier material settle or be flung outward.
decoy: Equipment for separating mixtures in labs, kitchens, mines and plants

members.title: Centrifuge
members.description: Lab rotor spinning sample tubes at thousands of revolutions per minute.

members.title: Separatory funnel
members.description: Pear-shaped glass vessel with a stopcock, shaken and then drained.

members.title: Cream separator
members.description: Hand-cranked dairy machine with a stack of spinning conical discs.

members.title: Gravy separator
members.description: Measuring jug with a spout that pours from the bottom.

members.title: Gold pan
members.description: Shallow ridged pan swirled in a creek by prospectors.

members.title: Sluice box
members.description: Long trough with riffles that catch flakes from flowing gravel.

members.title: Grease trap
members.description: Box under a restaurant sink that holds back fats from the drain.

members.title: Clarifier
members.description: Large round tank at a treatment works with a slow scraper arm.

members.title: Rocker box
members.description: Wooden cradle rocked by hand to wash gold-bearing gravel.

intruders.title: Magnetic separator
intruders.description: Drum or belt fitted with magnets over a recycling conveyor.
intruders.why: It pulls out iron and steel by magnetism, not density. It shares its name with the cream and gravy separators.

intruders.title: Fractionating column
intruders.description: Tall column packed with trays or beads above a boiling flask.
intruders.why: It splits liquids by boiling point. It is a classic separation apparatus beside the separatory funnel.

intruders.title: Chromatography column
intruders.description: Glass tube packed with silica through which a solvent is run.
intruders.why: It splits compounds by how strongly they cling to the packing, not by density. It is a standard lab separation tool.

theme: Objects that work as a wedge: a tapered piece forced into material or a gap to split, lift or hold it.
decoy: Everyday objects built around a sloping or tapering surface

members.title: Zipper
members.description: Slider that joins and parts two rows of interlocking teeth.

members.title: Doorstop
members.description: Rubber block kicked under a door to keep it open.

members.title: Shim
members.description: Thin sliver of wood slipped under a cabinet to level it.

members.title: Froe
members.description: L-shaped iron blade struck with a club to rive shingles.

members.title: Plow
members.description: Farm implement whose share turns over furrows of soil.

members.title: Nail
members.description: Pointed steel shank hammered into timber.

members.title: Wheel chock
members.description: Rubber block placed against a tire on a slope.

members.title: Splitting maul
members.description: Heavy blunt-edged head on a long handle, swung at firewood rounds.

intruders.title: Loading ramp
intruders.description: Sloped aluminum track for rolling a mower up into a truck.
intruders.why: A stationary inclined plane: the load moves along it, whereas a wedge is the part that moves. It is built on the same sloping surface.

intruders.title: Wood screw
intruders.description: Tapered steel fastener with a helical ridge and a slotted head.
intruders.why: A screw is an inclined plane wrapped around a shaft and is driven by turning. It has a pointed tip like a nail.
